judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-outs (particular design required by the Contract Documents; copyright violations in Owner- or Architect-prepared documents) are stated, though 'reason to believe' introduces a knowledge test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.5 makes royalties, licence fees and defence costs a reimbursable Cost of the Work and expressly turns on 'the last sentence of Subparagraph 3.17.1,' so who ultimately bears these costs depends on reading the two together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Arising out of or resulting from performance of the Work,' 'but only to the extent caused by the negligent acts or omissions,' and the survival of other indemnity rights are the standard battlegrounds of construction indemnity litigation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The indemnity is expressly limited to claims 'not covered by Project Management Protective Liability insurance purchased by the Contractor in accordance with Paragraph 11.3,' which is optional and which Article 16 (blank) never required; it also sits against the 4.3.10 consequential waiver and 11.4.7 subrogation waivers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short anti-limitation rule for workers' compensation defences; clearly expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supports 3.18.1; no contrary provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitional; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Architect is identified in the Agreement; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single rule requiring the written consent of Owner, Contractor and Architect to change the Architect's duties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 subjects every Architect approval to the Owner's express concurrence and Agreement 12.2.3 supersedes A201 9.4.1's timing—modifications of the Architect's authority made without any recorded Architect consent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The transcription is badly garbled, but the substance—a successor architect with the former Architect's status, subject to reasonable objection—is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.1.2 and the Agreement's identification of the Architect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Describes the Architect's administration role and limits authority to what the Contract Documents provide; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 adds an Owner consent layer to every Architect function, so the Architect's role as 'Owner's representative' is doubled up.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A disclaimer of Architect responsibility in conventional terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.1.3 and 4.2.2; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall endeavor to communicate ... through the Architect' is hortatory rather than mandatory, which itself invites argument about notices.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 requires direct written notice to and consent of the Owner wherever the Architect is involved, and 2.1.1.1 names Owner decision-makers, so routing of communications is stated two different ways.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The transcription is fragmentary but the function—evaluate applications and certify amounts due—is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.3 expressly supersedes A201 9.4.1's time periods for final certification, and Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1 adds a precondition to the final Certificate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long, carefully limited description of review 'only for the limited purpose of checking for conformance'; length is not ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1 requires Architect approval of all shop drawings, which fits within this review limitation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short statement of the Architect's Change Order authority.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 makes the Change Order the only route to a change in Contract Sum or Time except under 7.3 and 9.7.1, which narrows the minor-changes authority referenced here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Badly transcribed, but the function—determining Substantial Completion and issuing the final Certificate—is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1 bars the final Certificate until the Owner accepts all warranties, and Agreement 12.2.3 sets a different certification timetable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional on agreement between Owner and Architect; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No project representatives are identified in the Contract Documents, so the provision is dormant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 15-day rule for recognising delay is precise, though 'reasonable promptness' governs in the first instance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with 4.2.12 and 4.4.1; Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 adds Owner concurrence to interpretations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Consistent with the intent of and reasonably inferable from the Contract Documents' repeats the elastic standard of 1.2.1, and good-faith immunity is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with 4.4's claim procedure and Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1's Owner-concurrence requirement without direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Finality is granted and then qualified in the same sentence ('will be final if consistent with the intent expressed in the Contract Documents'), and 'aesthetic effect' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4.5.1 and 4.6.1 exclude aesthetic-effect claims from mediation and arbitration, while Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 reserves aesthetic control to the Owner—so who decides aesthetics, and where, is genuinely unsettled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition covering demands, assertions and 'other disputes and matters in question'; broad but deliberately so.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.4-4.6 and with Agreement 12.2.4's separate arbitration right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 21-day trigger is stated twice with a 'whichever is later' rule, but the clause never says whether compliance is a condition precedent to recovery.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 4.3.7.3 imposes further content requirements, Agreement 12.2.4 sets its own 30-day rule, and 4.3.4 has a parallel 21-day period; the notice regime is layered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear duty to continue performance and payment pending resolution, with two stated exceptions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires the Owner to 'continue to make payments' while 9.5.1 permits withholding certification and 12.1.7.5-.6 permit deductions, so the reach of the duty depends on those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Differ materially,' 'unknown physical conditions of an unusual nature,' and 'generally recognized as inherent in construction activities of the character provided for' are the classic differing-site-conditions phrases.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 allows Contract Sum changes only by Change Order, 1.2.1.1(b) allows no extra charge for dimensional differences, and in a cost-plus contract costs flow through anyway—three inconsistent treatments of extra cost.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'For reasons including but not limited to' followed by six enumerated grounds is precisely the general-versus-specific structure that generates ejusdem generis arguments.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 bars increases except by Change Order and the Agreement's cost-plus structure already passes cost through, so the claim grounds here need reconciling.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires written notice and an estimate of cost and probable effect; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Conditions 4.3.7.3 and 4.3.7.4 add detailed content requirements and a concurrent-delay bar, which supplement rather than contradict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Abnormal for the period of time' and 'could not have been reasonably anticipated' are evaluative tests that regularly produce disputes about weather claims.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 4.3.7.4's concurrent-delay bar interacts with weather claims, but there is no contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Within a reasonable time not exceeding 21 days' fixes an outer limit; the drafting is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.3.2 and the insurance articles.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Materially changed' and 'substantial inequity' are soft, but the remedy (equitable adjustment) is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 5.2.3 states no unit prices, so the provision operates only on prices 'subsequently agreed upon.'

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver's boundary—waived consequential damages including 'loss of profit except anticipated profit arising directly from the Work,' with liquidated direct damages preserved—is a much-litigated line.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.1 lets the Contractor recover a fee computed as if the Work were fully completed and A201 14.1.3 allows 'reasonable overhead, profit and damages,' which press against the waiver of profit and of termination-related consequential damages.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A menu of five permitted actions within ten days; precise, apart from the Architect's 'sole discretion' escape.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits 4.4.1 and 4.4.5; Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 adds Owner involvement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permissive consultation with a cost-allocation sentence; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.4.2 and 7.6.8's treatment of professional costs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A ten-day response requirement with three permitted responses; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.4.2 and 4.4.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Written decision, reasons, and 'final and binding ... but subject to mediation and arbitration' is an internally odd but well-understood formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with 4.4.6's 30-day demand rule and with Agreement 12.2.4, which permits arbitration without a further Architect decision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The consequence of failing to demand arbitration within 30 days is stated, though the condition ('when a written decision ... states that') makes the trigger depend on the Architect's drafting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.4 imposes a separate 30-day demand rule for final-accounting disputes and 4.6.3 adds a further limit, so three time bars operate on overlapping claims.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely permissive notice to the surety.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No surety or bond is required by Article 16, so the provision is largely dormant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short lien-preservation rule; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with Addendum 12.1.4(b) lien waivers and revised 12.2.2's lien-free endorsement condition, but consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Badly transcribed but substantively the standard AAA mediation procedure with a 60-day stay of arbitration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.4 lets the Contractor demand arbitration of the final-accounting dispute directly, which sits against 4.5.1's condition precedent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fee sharing, venue and enforceability of settlements; all definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 13.1.1 governing law; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exceptions (aesthetic effect and the 4.3.10, 9.10.4-9.10.5 waivers) are cross-referenced rather than described, and the transcription is fragmentary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Aesthetic claims are excluded here and made 'final' by 4.2.13 subject to a consistency proviso, while Agreement 12.2.4 permits arbitration outside this route; the dispute architecture is not fully harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies the rules and the filing requirements precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.4's demand mechanism and 4.4.6's time limit interlock with this; no contradiction in the filing mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The outer limit—no demand after the date when legal proceedings 'would be barred by the applicable statute of limitations as determined pursuant to Paragraph 13.7'—stacks three cross-references and is hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13.7.1 fixes accrual dates by project milestone and 4.4.6 and Agreement 12.2.4 add 30-day bars, so the limitation scheme has several moving parts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dense series of negatives about consolidation and joinder, turning on phrases such as 'substantially involved in a common question of fact or law whose presence is required if complete relief is to be accorded.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Architect is not a party to the Agreement yet performs decisive functions, and Agreement 12.2.4 contemplates arbitration of accounting disputes; joinder questions therefore arise naturally.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence enforcement provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.6.2 and 13.1.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitional; the exclusion of separate contractors is express.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Agreement Article 10 and A201 6.1.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitional; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.3.1 flow-down requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Failure of the Owner or Architect to reply promptly shall constitute notice of no reasonable objection' converts silence into consent without defining 'promptly.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 10.1 gives the Owner power to designate bidders and to determine which bids are accepted, and Addendum 6.5 requires at least two bids including Owner- or Architect-named subcontractors—a materially different selection process.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable and timely objection' is soft but conventional, and the reciprocal right is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 10.1's final sentence states the same reciprocal right, and Addendum 6.5 requires named subcontractors to be 'reasonably acceptable to Contractor.'

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The adjustment turns on whether the rejected subcontractor was 'reasonably capable of performing the Work' and on the Contractor having 'acted promptly and responsively.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 10.2 provides a different remedy for Owner-forced bid substitution measured by the difference in bids and adjusting the Guaranteed Maximum Price; two remedies for similar facts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line restriction; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.2.1-5.2.3 and Agreement 10.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A contingent assignment with three conditions; the mechanism is dense but each condition is stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.3 requires the Contractor to execute assignments as a condition of receiving termination payments, and 14.2.2 lets the Owner accept assignment; the routes overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Equitable adjustment of the subcontractor's compensation after suspension; short and standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Agreement 13.4 and A201 14.3.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reserves the Owner's right to self-perform or award separate contracts, with a claim route for the Contractor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement Article 2 excepts work indicated to be others' responsibility; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional convention for multiple contracts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No separate contracts are identified; dormant but consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Coordination duties with a mechanism for revising the construction schedule by joint review and mutual agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4 and 3.10.5 make the Construction Schedule a Contract Document revised by Contractor and Architect at design phases, a different process from the joint review with separate contractors described here.
